title: Advocates ‘heartbroken’ by alleged rape of client who was in disability provider’s care
summary: Advocates are “deeply disturbed” and “heartbroken” over the alleged neglect at a  community provide in Baltimore that resulted in the rape and impregnation of a young woman with significant cognitive disabilities.
content:
by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters May 6, 2026

by Danielle J. Brown, Maryland Matters May 6, 2026

Advocates are “deeply disturbed” and “heartbroken” over the alleged neglect at a  community provider in Baltimore that resulted in the rape and impregnation of a young woman with significant cognitive disabilities.

Carin Smith, co-founder of the Concerned Citizens of Self-Direction Maryland, said that as a mother of a 28-year-old daughter who receives developmental disability services, the case “really hits home.”

“When you have a child that doesn’t speak, especially a young woman that can get pregnant – I mean, that’s exactly what you fear,” Smith said. “We’re all grieving for [the plaintiff] and her family … we’re heartbroken.”

A negligence lawsuit, first reported  Tuesday by the Washington Post, claims that a young woman was sexually abused while in the care of Baltimore-based community service provider Dominion Resource Center, resulting in the patient getting pregnant some time in April 2024 and the birth of a child in December 2024.

The plaintiff’s significant developmental disabilities leave her incapable of consenting to sexual acts, according to the lawsuit that claims she was “sexually abused, sexually tortured, raped and impregnated and forced to carry to term causing tremendous anguish, unnecessary physical harm, pain, suffering, emotional distress and trauma.”

The rapist is still unknown, but the plaintiff’s parents, Marcia Williams and Kevin Jones, are suing state officials and the service providers for negligence and failing to ensure the plaintiff was “safe and protected from abuse, neglect and exploitation.” States Newsroom does not identify victims of sexual assault in its reporting.

The lawsuit represents another painful hit to the developmental disabilities community, which is undergoing a second year of significant budget cuts to the Developmental Disabilities Administration that advocates say will threaten disability care.

The Maryland Association of Community Services, of which Dominion Resource Center is a member, says that it is “deeply disturbed” about the alleged sexual assault and supports a thorough investigation by all appropriate authorities.

“We stand with the victim and all people with disabilities who depend on Maryland’s community services system for their safety and care,” according to the association’s written statement issued Tuesday.

“While this reported incident is deeply troubling, it does not reflect the dedication and compassion of the vast majority of providers and their employees across Maryland, who come to work every day genuinely committed to serving, supporting, and caring for people with developmental disabilities,” the statement said.

The plaintiff at the center of the case is “wheelchair bound, legally blind, neurogenically incontinent of bowel and bladder and has limited verbal expression” and cognitively “functions at the level of a young toddler,” according to the lawsuit. She requires significant hands-on care for her daily activities and wore a safety smock that covered her abdomen to prevent her from disrobing and tearing her clothes due to a behavioral health disorder.

The plaintiff has received health and behavioral care coverage through Maryland Medicaid’s Community Pathway Waiver program since 2021 and received disability services at the Baltimore-based Milford Home, owned and operated by Dominion Resource Center.

Dominion Resource Center is a not-for-profit licensed provider for developmental disability services through a Medicaid waiver, receiving state and federal funding for doing so. The waiver program is operated by the Maryland Department of Health’s Developmental Disabilities Administration, and the Office of Health Care Quality is responsible for completing compliance surveys for service providers.

The lawsuit says that on or about April 10, 2024, the plaintiff was raped and impregnated, despite her health care plan recommending that she have two staff members attending her, with one within 10 feet of her all times when she was awake, and within hearing distance when she was asleep, checking on her every 30 minutes. The suit alleges that she was either left alone without her staff or left in the presence of a male attendant for her care when the rape occurred.

But her pregnancy would not be documented until Nov. 10, when the plaintiff was taken to Sinai Hospital’s emergency department for “abdominal pain and swelling” and an ultrasound discovered a single fetus at an estimated gestational age of 30 weeks.

Upon the discovery of the plaintiff’s pregnancy, the hospital reported the rape and sexual abuse to the Baltimore City Police and state officials.

In April of this year, the plaintiff’s family filed a lawsuit with the Circuit Court for Baltimore City, claiming that staff connected with Dominion Resource Center and related companies were negligent with her care and conspired to hide the pregnancy.

The lawsuit claims that staff tasked with bathing her, changing her clothes, and providing genital hygiene care would have noticed bodily changes due to pregnancy, including a swelling stomach and changes in breast size, in the seven months her pregnancy was not documented.

Lawmakers faced increased ‘harassment’ over DDA budget cuts, as advocates faced impacts

Meanwhile, health care records noted medical and behavioral changes in the months between April 2024 and November 2024, including irregular menstrual cycles, changes in eating preferences and vomiting, during the plaintiff’s regular and frequent health care exams. But those symptoms were not followed up with adequate examinations to detect the pregnancy, the lawsuit says, even though it was likely that staff were aware of the pregnancy by October 2024, if not months earlier.

The lawsuit claims eight counts of negligence by state officials, Dominion Resource Center, a company responsible with arranging developmental disabilities services, and staff members involved in the care of the plaintiff.

Three staff members are named for intentional infliction of emotional distress, civil conspiracy and punitive damages. The lawsuit calls for punitive damages and costs “in excess of $75,000” for each of the 11 counts outlined in the court document.

Dominion Resource Center did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday, but an official with the company told the Washington Post that six of its staffers had been cleared in the incident, which she said “really breaks my heart.”

The Department of Health said it could not comment on ongoing litigation.

“Investigations of complaints regarding services for Marylanders who participate in DDA waiver programs have been and continue to be a priority for the Moore-Miller Administration,” department spokesperson Amanda Hils said in a written statement. “The Maryland Department of Health’s goal is to provide a sustainable, accessible and effective program of meaningful services for Marylanders with disabilities.”

This story was updated on Wednesday, May 6, to correct the state officials that Sinai Hospital reported the rape to.
